title: Divinity of Christ
english: When the Lord took on humanity, he would make human things and would not despise the measures of humanity, but would be like those who are human, and prophecy would be counted among the highest things, and it is said clearly that he who is to be born will have a place of dignity among human things, but if someone were to concede that he is a prophet like himself, from humans, but not from God, then we will not say that the Son is by nature God, and we will show that he is from God according to nature.

Moses, as a prophet and a man, is thought to have spoken according to his own nature, but he is actually ignorant of the truth. Only the prophesied one will rise, and Moses, despite being a prophet, erred in his understanding. Nothing else is certain except this. Many prophets came before Moses, and they were all men who spoke about him, but they strayed from the truth. For he will immediately subject, he says, not all necessity is thus, that I, according to some, should think in many ways about us.

Moses' power is something that we should strive to understand, particularly in relation to the ministry of the Savior's dispensation. He liberated the Israelites from their heavy servitude, leading them through the middle of the sea and nourishing them in the wilderness.

The mediator stood by God, guiding humanity to all good deeds and wisely composing them to all honesty. From the type and shadow, he led them to the truth, but Satan exercised tyranny over us, exploiting our greed and binding the human race with the yoke of sin.

No one was completely free from Satan's perversity, and he insulted the weakness of all, boasting that he would seize the whole world and lift it like abandoned eggs, and that no one could escape or contradict him. But he was wrong to think no one would contradict him.

The Lord thought to trample the earth with his feet, but Christ put the heaven under his feet, and in doing so, he freed us from the bondage of the soul and the depths of sin. Through his power, he led us through the Jordan.
Christ gave us himself as holy and life-giving food, and he became a mediator between God and humans.

The divine law has been revealed to humanity, and it is through this law that we come to understand the truth. Moses, who was given the task of writing down the laws, knew that the only-begotten Word of God would surpass all human life and give better laws to humans. As he wrote about the laws, he made it clear that nothing should be added or taken away from them, and that they should be obeyed in all things. This is because the law itself has a form of divine truth, which has now been revealed to us.

The Word of God has taken on humanity and given us a new understanding of the law. As we obey the law and follow the teachings of the Word of God, we come to know the truth and experience the divine majesty and glory.

The lawgiver, as he says, has the right to establish laws, and this is evident in the prophecy of Moses about Christ, which God the Father himself confirmed. For it is written that God will raise up a prophet like Moses, and this prophet will speak the words that God gives him.

In this way, God declares that he alone has the authority to establish laws, and that no one else is worthy of this authority. As the master, he has the power to establish laws, and his words are the only ones that truly matter.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be fragmented, and some sentences may be cut off mid-thought.
The translation of 'ὑποθεῖναι ποσὶ thy On’ οὐρανόν' is uncertain, but it seems to describe Christ's action of putting the heaven under his feet.
The phrase 'ἐλπίδος 6δείλαιος' is difficult to translate, but it appears to describe the state of the person who has lost hope.
The text contains allusions to Psalm 107:20 and Deuteronomy 18:15.
The translation of 'λαqueos' is uncertain, but it seems to refer to a snare or trap.
The text contains a possible reference to the Jordan River, but the context is unclear.
The edge cuts in the source are noted, but the translation does not attempt to complete or invent missing words.
